newsitem.title: USA: Quest Medical sees line's revs growing.
newsitem.headline: Quest Medical sees line's revs growing.

text.p: Quest Medical Inc said Wednesday it expected revenues from its leading product line to grow by more than 20 percent during the second half of its fiscal year -- the same rate at which it has grown during the first.

Quest said in a statement it had seen strong market demand for its Advanced Neuromodulation System ever since it came out last March with an improved design for the line's products. It said it had received Australian and European approvals for the line's products during the second quarter.
Robert Merrill, the company's senior vice president-finance, said the line was responsible for about half of Quest's revenues during the first six months of the year.
The line's products include catheters and receivers that are made to be implanted in a patient to help eliminate chronic back pain, among other discomforts.
Quest reported a net loss of $35,000 for the second quarter against a profit of $114,000. The loss was incurred after writing off the inventory of the line's old products, it said.

The company also said it expected to finalize its plans for a strategic alliance or some other business deal by the end of the third quarter of 1997. In March 1997, it hired Smith Barney and Rauscher Pierce Refsnes as investment bankers to seek strategic alternatives such as a strategic alliance, sale of a business unit, or sale of the entire company.
Quest Medical makes a variety of healthcare products used primarily in cardiovascular surgery, neurostimulation and intravenous fluid delivery applications.
